A common path is: secondary vocational or associate degree in emergency care/nursing -> earn emergency responder or EMT credentials -> gain field experience as an EMT -> advance to paramedic -> move into emergency-department or flight-paramedic work.

paragraphs: After receiving a dispatch, listen to the chief complaint and determine the response level. At the scene, assess while performing CPR or establishing access and administering medication, then lift the patient into the ambulance and monitor oxygen saturation and blood pressure en route. Relay the condition by phone so the emergency department can prepare, then transfer the patient directly to the resuscitation room. Back at the station, disinfect and maintain equipment and write records. When a life cannot be saved, paramedics must also recover emotionally.
